name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
principle: The product writes user-controlled data into a CRLF-delimited output without rejecting, encoding, or quoting CR or LF. Downstream parsers treat injected line breaks as real record boundaries, allowing attacker-created headers, responses, log entries, or variables.
detection_signals: Java `response.addHeader(name, request.getParameter(...))` or `response.setHeader(name, tainted)` without CR/LF validation
Java `response.sendRedirect(tainted)` or `setStatus` plus `Location: ` header built from tainted data
Java `new Cookie(name, request.getParameter(...))` followed by `response.addCookie(cookie)` without CR/LF validation
`logger.info/debug/error(... + request.getParameter(...))` or `printf`/`fprintf(log, "%s", tainted)` without CR/LF escaping
SMTP/mail header construction like `"Subject: " + tainted + "\r\n"` or `addHeader("From", tainted)` without CR/LF validation
Raw socket/stream writes of text protocol headers: `write("Header: " + tainted + "\r\n")`
CI/env-file writes such as `echo "NAME=$(cat file)" >> $GITHUB_ENV` where file content is attacker-controlled
negative_signals: Input is rejected by `contains("\r") || contains("\n")` or equivalent before reaching the header/log/mail/env sink
Input is allowlisted with a full-string pattern such as `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` before reaching the CRLF-delimited sink
CR and LF are encoded or escaped before output, e.g. `.replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\n", "\\n")` for logs
Header value is selected from a server-side enum/map and not copied from request data
Framework API documents and enforces rejection of CR/LF in the specific sink, and exceptions are handled by aborting output
false_defense_traps: Filtering only literal `\r\n` while accepting lone `\r`, lone `\n`, `%0d`, `%0a`, or decoded equivalents
Validating before URL/HTML/entity decoding while the sink receives decoded data
Client-side JavaScript validation without identical server-side validation
Using a standard header/log API but prebuilding a raw multi-line header string before passing it
Removing CR/LF only for HTTP headers while the same tainted value is also written to logs, SMTP, or `$GITHUB_ENV`
verification_focus: Can attacker-controlled data containing CR or LF reach any CRLF-delimited sink before canonicalization and neutralization?

consequence_chains.trigger: CRLF reaches an HTTP request or response header value
consequence_chains.consequence: HTTP header injection or response splitting

consequence_chains.trigger: CRLF reaches a log message sink
Newline injection creates a CI environment variable such as `NODE_OPTIONS`
consequence_chains.consequence: Code execution in the workflow runner

patch_principle: Avoid designs that use attacker-controlled text inside CRLF-delimited control fields.
Canonicalize/decode input before validation, then reject CR, LF, and other control characters.
Use strict allowlists for structured fields such as cookie values, header values, IDs, and PR numbers.
Escape CR and LF when preserving free-form text in logs or records.
Use framework APIs that enforce CR/LF rejection, and fail closed on validation exceptions.

minimal_examples.safe: String name = request.getParameter("name"); if (name.matches(".*[\\r\\n].*")) throw new IllegalArgumentException(); response.setHeader("X-Name", name);
